A 68-year-old woman comes to the emergency department with symptoms of weight loss, abdominal
pain, and jaundice. A CT scan reveals a mass in the head of the pancreas, and a biopsy is scheduled
for the following day. Outside the patient’s room, her daughter requests that the biopsy results not be
disclosed to the patient. Instead, she asks that the results be shared with her and her brother, who is
the patient’s designated health care proxy. She explains that they have agreed it would be best for the
patient not to be told about a cancer diagnosis. The biopsy performed the next morning confirms
pancreatic adenocarcinoma. What is the most appropriate response to the daughter’s request? Answer
Choices: (A) Explain that the diagnosis must be shared unless the patient lacks decision-making
capacity (B) Tell the patient's daughter that the patient must be informed of the diagnosis (C) Refer the
matter to the hospital ethics committee before proceeding (D) Ask the patient's son, the documented
health care proxy, how he would like to handle the situation (E) Document the family's request and
comply with their wishes (F) Consult with legal counsel regarding the hospital's liability in this situation
(G) Suggest psychological evaluation of the patient before disclosure (H) Agree to withhold the

diagnosis since the healthcare proxy has made this decision (I) Delay disclosure until a comprehensive
treatment plan is developed (J) Inquire why the patient's daughter feels her mother should not be
informed of the diagnosis
 A. Refer the matter to the hospital ethics committee before proceeding
B. Consult with legal counsel regarding the hospital's liability in this situation
C. Ask the patient's son, the documented health care proxy, how he would like to handle the
situation
D. Delay disclosure until a comprehensive treatment plan is developed
E. Suggest psychological evaluation of the patient before disclosure
F. Agree to withhold the diagnosis since the healthcare proxy has made this decision
G. Document the family's request and comply with their wishes
H. Inquire why the patient's daughter feels her mother should not be informed of the diagnosis
I. Tell the patient's daughter that the patient must be informed of the diagnosis
J. Explain that the diagnosis must be shared unless the patient lacks decision-making capacity
